proof_summary: Writing \(p=2h+1\), reflection and the congruence \((1+X)^p\equiv1+X^p\pmod p\) show that all entries with \(p\le i+j<2p-1\) vanish: odd-index sums cancel by reflection, while the remaining sums cancel after pairing their \(k\) and \(p+k\) parts (with the corresponding central-binomial congruences for the second sum). At index \(p-1\), \(\binom{p-1}{k}\equiv(-1)^k\) gives the values \(1\) and \((-1)^h\), respectively (only the middle term survives in the latter); reversing the columns therefore makes each Hankel matrix triangular, and its reversal sign \((-1)^h\) together with the constant diagonal gives the claimed residues.
